job.title: Environmental, Health & Safety Compliance Officer
job.description:
Environmental & Compliance Officer
  
About the opportunity
  
This is an opportunity to join an established resource recovery and waste management operation in South Western Sydney, where environmental compliance, safety and operational excellence are critical to ongoing success. Reporting to senior management, the Environmental and Compliance Officer will play a key role in ensuring the site operates in accordance with EPA licence conditions, development approvals, environmental legislation and WHS requirements.
This is a hands on, site based position suited to someone who enjoys being close to operations, identifying risks before they become issues, and working collaboratively with teams to maintain high standards of environmental and safety performance. You will have the opportunity to influence real outcomes, strengthen systems and help maintain the organisation's licence to operate.
  
What you will be doing:
  
This is a diverse role with broad responsibility across environmental compliance, risk management and workplace safety, including:
  
  • Managing compliance with NSW EPA Environment Protection Licence (EPL) conditions and requirements
  • Maintaining compliance registers, monitoring obligations and ensuring key actions are completed on time
  • Monitoring environmental risks including waste handling, stockpiling, water management, dust, odour, noise, litter and air quality
  • Coordinating EPA reporting, inspections, audits, notifications and regulatory correspondence
  • Investigating environmental incidents, non-compliances and corrective actions
  • Conducting site inspections and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement
  • Reviewing environmental performance data and implementing corrective actions where required
  • Monitoring waste acceptance processes and ensuring compliance with approved waste categories
  
About you
  • You are a practical and detail focused environmental professional who enjoys working within an operational environment and being visible on site.
  • You understand how to balance regulatory obligations with operational realities and are confident interpreting environmental requirements and translating them into practical actions. You build credibility with operational teams, communicate effectively at all levels and take a proactive approach to identifying and managing risk.
  • Most importantly, you are someone who enjoys ownership, values accountability, and wants to make a genuine contribution to environmental and safety performance.
  
What you will bring
  • Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Environmental Engineering, Sustainability or a related discipline
  • Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety or equivalent
  • Approximately 3 to 5 years of experience in environmental compliance, WHS or operational environmental roles
  • Experience interpreting environmental approvals, licence conditions and regulatory requirements
  • Strong capability in inspections, risk assessments, compliance monitoring and documentation
  • Experience managing environmental incidents, investigations and corrective actions
  • Confidence engaging with regulators, consultants and operational stakeholders
  • Strong written communication and reporting skills
  
  
Why Join?
  • This is an opportunity to step into a broad and influential compliance role where your work will be visible and valued.
  • You will join a collaborative organisation that is committed to maintaining high environmental and safety standards while continuing to support operational performance. With exposure to a diverse range of compliance, risk and improvement activities, this role offers the opportunity to build your expertise, take ownership and make a meaningful impact across the business.
About Applying

At TSS, we embrace individuality and differences in gender, age, ethnicity, race, cultural background, disability, faith and sexual orientation. We strive to provide a recruitment experience that’s fair, inclusive and accessible. We encourage all suitable applicants to apply for this role.
For any accessibility needs to be considered during the recruitment process, please let us know at support@thesafestep.com.au
                       
For a confidential discussion, please contact John Spring at jspring@thesafestep.com.au or click “Apply” to apply for this role.

job.title: Group Risk and Retail Protections Manager

An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Group Risk & Retail Protection Manager to lead the organisation's enterprise risk, retail protection and asset protection strategy.  As the business continues to evolve, this role presents an outstanding opportunity to join a high-performing leadership team and make a genuine impact. This is a rare opportunity to join a dynamic organisation at an exciting point in its evolution, influence strategy, build strong stakeholder relationships, and contribute to the ongoing success.
  
About the Role
This leadership role will partner closely with the executive team to reduce retail loss, strengthen operational discipline and embed practical risk management across the business. This is a commercially focused role where success will be measured by tangible improvements in shrink, loss prevention, risk management, and business performance and continuity.
  
Leading a specialist team, you will develop and deliver an integrated risk and retail protection strategy that protects people, property and assets while supporting informed commercial decision-making.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading the risk and retail protection function across a large retail network.

job.title: Group Safety Leader
job.description:
About Domino’s

Domino’s Pizza Enterprises is one of the world's largest and most recognised quick service restaurant (QSR) brands, operating across multiple international markets and serving millions of customers every week.

The organisation is entering a new phase, including the appointment of a new Group CEO. With a focus on growth, innovation and operational improvement, Domino’s is continuing to invest in the systems, capability and leadership needed to support its next stage.

Safety is an important part of this work. With a large network of stores, delivery drivers and operational teams, there are a range of safety challenges to manage across different countries and operating environments.

This is an opportunity to join Domino’s Pizza Enterprises in a newly created Group Safety Lead role, working across 12 countries and a large, diverse operational network.

The role will suit a safety professional who is ready to broaden their experience and take on greater responsibility across a large international organisation. You will work closely with senior leaders and safety teams across different markets, helping to develop consistent approaches to safety, improve reporting and governance, and share good practice across the business.

It is a role where you can use your existing safety experience while continuing to develop your leadership, stakeholder management and international experience.
  
About the Role
Reporting initially to the Group CEO, the Group Safety Lead will provide safety leadership and subject matter expertise across 12 countries, including Australia, New Zealand, Asia and Europe.

You will work with local safety and operational teams to help develop the Group Safety Strategy, improve governance and reporting, and support a more consistent approach to managing risk.

The role will cover areas including delivery and road safety, fleet and driver risk, safety capability, risk management, reporting and sharing better ways of working across the organisation.

You won't be expected to do this through a large team. Much of the role will involve working with people across the business, building relationships, providing practical advice and helping local teams identify opportunities to improve.

This is a good opportunity for someone who enjoys working with operational teams and wants to gain broader experience across a complex, international organisation.

About You

You will have a background in health and safety and be comfortable working with operational leaders and teams. You may currently be working as a Safety Manager, Senior Safety Advisor, HSE Business Partner or in a similar role and be looking for an opportunity to take the next step.

You will be someone who can build relationships, communicate clearly and turn safety requirements into practical solutions. You don't need to have worked in a global organisation before, but experience across multiple sites, jurisdictions or operational environments would be useful.

Experience in QSR, retail, transport, logistics, franchising, consumer services, aviation, infrastructure or other operationally intensive environments would be relevant. Exposure to road, driver, rider or fleet safety would also be well regarded.

Most importantly, you will be curious, practical and comfortable working with different people and perspectives. You will enjoy being part of a business where you can see the impact of your work and continue developing your own leadership capability.

If you are looking for an opportunity to broaden your safety experience, work with a well-known Australian brand and gain exposure to an international operation, this could be an interesting next step.

About You

Lead the next chapter of Casey's Health, Safety & Wellbeing journey and help create a safer, healthier and more resilient future.

job.title: Head of HSE Operations
job.description:
HEAD OF HSEQ OPERATIONS

National Executive Safety Leadership Opportunity (based in Brisbane/Sydney or Melbourne)

ABOUT THE COMPANY

An established and nationally recognised Australian transport organisation is seeking an experienced safety leader to join its senior leadership team.
Operating across multiple jurisdictions, the organisation delivers essential public services through a geographically dispersed workforce and complex, high-risk operational environments. Safety is fundamental to its success, and the business has established a strong safety culture and industry-leading safety outcomes relative to its peer group.

Continued growth, the integration of new operations and increasing complexity across the risk landscape have created an opportunity for a senior safety professional to influence safety performance at a national level.
This is also an organisation that invests in its people, with genuine succession pathways and opportunities for high-performing leaders to progress into broader executive roles.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting directly to the General Manager HSEQ, the Head of HSEQ Operations is a pivotal national leadership position responsible for driving consistency, capability, governance and continual improvement across the organisation.

This is not a desk-bound corporate safety role. The successful candidate will combine strategic thinking with strong operational credibility, working closely with Managing Directors, operational leaders and regional safety teams to identify emerging risks and deliver practical improvements.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Analyse safety data, trends and leading indicators to identify emerging and high-consequence risks.
  • Develop and implement national safety improvement initiatives.
  • Strengthen consistency across safety systems, processes and standards.
  • Lead and support major incident and ICAM investigations, ensuring organisational learning is embedded.
  • Provide assurance across integrated management systems, ISO frameworks, compliance and audit programs.
  • Consolidate and interpret national safety data to provide meaningful insight to Executive and Board stakeholders.
  • Mentor and develop regional safety leaders and build safety capability across the organisation.
  • Partner with operational leaders to deliver sustainable improvements while balancing governance with commercial and operational realities.
The role has significant national influence, including a dotted-line leadership relationship with regional safety professionals across multiple operating divisions.

ABOUT YOU

You will be an experienced safety leader who is comfortable operating in complex, high-risk and geographically dispersed environments.
You are likely to bring:
  • Significant senior HSEQ leadership experience across transport, rail, logistics, infrastructure, construction, mining, manufacturing or another comparable high-risk industry.
  • Strong operational risk management capability, ideally including heavy vehicle or transport-related risk.
  • Experience with ISO-certified management systems, audit and assurance.
  • Proven ICAM and serious incident investigation capability.
  • Experience working across multiple sites, jurisdictions and diverse operational cultures.
  • Strong analytical capability, with the ability to turn safety data into meaningful business insight.
  • The credibility to influence senior executives while remaining connected to frontline operations.
Most importantly, you will be a practical, collaborative and emotionally mature leader who builds relationships before implementing change.
You will be confident challenging constructively, comfortable operating under pressure and capable of influencing without relying on authority. You will understand that effective safety leadership is ultimately about earning trust, building capability and helping operational leaders achieve better outcomes.
This is an exceptional opportunity for a senior safety professional who wants to move beyond functional leadership and make a genuine national impact, while positioning themselves for future broader executive leadership opportunities.

job.title: Senior Psychosocial Risk & Wellbeing Manager

Significant foundational work has already been completed, including frameworks, tools, risk assessment methodologies and supporting resources. The challenge now is to bring these components together into a cohesive operating model, drive organisation wide adoption and deliver measurable outcomes.
This is not a traditional wellbeing role. It is a strategic leadership opportunity focused on embedding mature psychosocial risk practices across a large and complex organisation.

  • Lead implementation and continuous improvement of the Health & Wellbeing Framework.
  • Drive a proactive psychosocial risk management program across the organisation.
  • Develop consistent approaches to triage, risk assessment, controls and case management.

  • Influence and partner with senior leaders and specialist functions to deliver coordinated responses to complex psychosocial matters.
  • Strengthen organisational capability through coaching, education and stakeholder engagement.
